s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly growing caruncular lesion with ulceration
salient_findings: Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with ulcerated surface
Large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
key_facts: Male patient in his late 60s
4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
Medical and ocular histories were unremarkable
Ocular examination findings were normal except for the caruncular lesion
No evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
Specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm with a 4-mm ulceration
Necrotic tissue on the surface of the specimen
Solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface
Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Significant number of cycling cells shown by Ki-67 proliferation marker
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma of the caruncle
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly growing, ulcerated caruncular lesion with positive melanocytic markers

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerated lesion, although less likely given positive melanocytic markers

shortlist.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive growth pattern, but less likely given specific melanocytic marker positivity

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely due to rapid growth and ulceration, but still a consideration for caruncular lesions

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and ulceration, but less likely given specific histopathological and immunohistochemical findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, and pedunculated mass with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and a high proliferative index, as indicated by Ki-67 staining, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific markers for squamous cell carcinoma and presence of melanocytic markers

rejected.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
rejected.why: No indication of sebaceous gland origin in the histopathology or immunohistochemistry results

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typical basal cell carcinoma features, such as palisading nuclei, were not mentioned

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of neuroendocrine markers or features typical of Merkel cell carcinoma
